summary: evt-dispatcher ships a native dropper that executes a bundled opaque payload on require
details: The package advertises itself as a lightweight pure-JS event dispatcher but ships two prebuilt native addons (native.napi.node for Linux, native_win.node for Windows) plus a 1.3 MB high-entropy opaque file named.napi_cache at the package root. index.js unconditionally require()s the native addon at the top of the module (repeated five times inside try/catch to maximize load reliability) before declaring a trivial EventBus class. On require, the native addon reads the bundled.napi_cache blob, writes the decoded bytes to /tmp/.<pid>, chmods the file, and spawns it as a detached process via fork + setsid + execlp, giving the installer arbitrary native code execution that persists beyond the Node process. The native loader also contains dedicated anti-analysis logic with no benign purpose in an event-emitter: it enumerates CI/sandbox environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SANDBOX), reads /proc/1/cgroup for docker/containerd/kubepod/podman markers, checks /proc/self/status TracerPid, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent / CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and scans running processes for wireshark and httpdebug. No binding.gyp, C sources, or install hooks are declared, and the shipped JS has no legitimate need for native code — the native addon is a decoder/dropper for the opaque payload, and the JS is a cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
